quote: Die Formen $f$ und $g$ gegeben; Gesucht $\varphi$, so dass $(f\varphi)_i^n=\lambda(g\varphi)_k^m$. $n=2i$, $m=2k$ (und die Constanten)
english: The forms f and g are given; sought: $\varphi$ such that $(f\varphi)_i^n=\lambda(g\varphi)_k^m$, with n=2i, m=2k (and the constants).
topic: A list of research topics and problems on binary forms, covariants, invariants, the principle of special position, and the three-body problem.

triage.modern_statement: Let f be a binary form of degree n = 2i and g a binary form of degree m = 2k. The notation (fφ)_i is read here as the classical i-th transvectant (Überschiebung). Since i = n/2 and k = m/2, these are the 'middle' transvectants: for a binary form φ of degree p, both (f,φ)_i and (g,φ)_k have degree p again. So each one defines an SL2-equivariant linear operator, T_f and T_g, on the space V_p of binary p-ic forms. The problem asks for all φ and constants λ with T_f(φ) = λ·T_g(φ). In modern terms this is a generalized eigenvalue problem for a pencil of operators: the admissible λ are the roots of det(T_f − λT_g) = 0, and φ ranges over the corresponding eigenspaces. Hilbert's '(and the constants)' presumably means determining the λ, whose characteristic polynomial has coefficients that are joint invariants of f and g. This reading is my own and is not taken from a source.
triage.answered_by: No identifiable later answer was found. Two web searches turned up no paper, edition, or commentary that discusses this diary entry or this exact problem (proportional middle transvectants (f,φ)_{n/2} = λ(g,φ)_{m/2}). Part of the question is basic linear algebra once it is stated as an eigenvalue problem. Any deeper classical treatment (for example, explicit forms of the eigencovariants φ or of the invariants controlling λ) may exist in the 19th-century invariant-theory literature, but I could not confirm it. The search budget ran out before I could check further, including a planned follow-up search on Chipalkatti's paper.

evidence.claim: The k-th transvectant (A,B)_k of binary forms A and B, of orders p and q, is the image of A⊗B under the projection in the Clebsch–Gordan decomposition. This is the standard modern setting for transvectant operators like those in Hilbert's note.
Hilbert's dissertation was on invariant properties of special binary forms, especially spherical functions. This places the note within his early invariant-theory interests.

Hilbert's notebooks (Cod. Ms. Hilbert 600) contain many undated research notes. Historians have studied them mainly in connection with the 24th problem, which is about simplicity of proofs and is unrelated to this entry.
Hilbert's notebooks are being studied and edited, but no source I found discusses this entry.

triage.why: The entry is precise enough to restate as an equivariant generalized eigenvalue problem for transvectant operators on binary forms, but that restatement is my own reading. It is not among Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. I found no source showing that this specific question was posed, studied, or solved later. Classical invariant theory is still studied today through transvectants and Clebsch–Gordan theory, but I found no current research on this particular problem. A partial answer is elementary, since the λ are roots of a determinant whose coefficients are joint invariants. Even so, I cannot cite a source that treats it, so I classify it as possibly unexplored, with low confidence.
